comparison.reading: A2/A3 rows are two-rank all-reduce on their own measured campaigns and are reproduced here with the same affine convention; the A5 rows come from this artifact.  A 2-rank collective is limited by one die-pair path, which is why A2 r2 < A3 r2 < A5 r8 and why the A5 r2 all-reduce (47 GB/s at 128MiB) sits close to the A5 single-die-pair P2P rate (~50 GB/s) rather than to the A5 8-rank aggregate (~133 GB/s).

gaps.detail: no RoCE/scale-out payload was measured; npu-smi topo reports every NIC as NA and all five blocks are single-host. Any W>8 or cross-host prediction is uncovered by this artifact.
only W=2 and W=8 were measured; W=4 and W=16 curves cannot be derived without an interpolation rule this campaign did not measure.

bf16 only; the msprof engine phase never produced an engine block in any salvaged parent record, so engine == not_observed (A2's campaign did capture ffts_plus_ai_core). No fp8/HiSparse engine point exists.

gaps.gap: collectives with no repo lane mode
gaps.detail: all_gather, reduce_scatter and all_to_all are measured here but a3_communication.CommCondition only has all_reduce_only / p2p_only / all_reduce_plus_p2p; they are published as measured rows and excluded from comm_conditions rather than forced into all_reduce_only.

the A2/A3 campaigns measured the overlapped MC2 lane; the A5 campaign ran each collective in isolation, so the UB overlap/contention rule is still unknown (comm.py keeps UB channel_semantics == unknown).
repetitions=1 conditions have a much larger per-op cost than the fitted alpha; they are published as launch-inclusive evidence and excluded from the fit, matching the A2/A3 convention.
